newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 19.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Traders expect market to surge further on follow-through and selective buying.

* Improved turnover and buying on Wednesday in real estate issues which have been battered by negative sentiment indicate a return of confidence in the market which will likely be sustained, Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president Noel Reyes.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed 25.10 points higher at 2,823.35 points.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 42.07 points lower at 7,718.71. PLDT's ADR closed $0 1/4 lower at $63 1/2.
* The peso closed lower at 26.379 to the dollar vs 26.375
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rose at 13.0625 percent vs 13.03125 percent.

* The Securities and Exchange Commission said it will conduct further investigation into alleged price manipulation on property issues by traders saying its initial findings were insufficient to arrive at a conclusion.

* Property firm Empire East Land Holdings Inc said it has purchased 6.356 million of its own shares at three pesos a share from the market. Empire posted gains the past two sessions owing to a 6.356 million share buyback and rumours of a takeover, which the company denied.
* President Fidel Ramos said in a speech in London that the Philippine government expects to achieve gross national product (GNP) growth of at least 7.0 percent this year.
* President Ramos reaffirmed in London he would not run for a second term but said he would to continue to act as an elder statesman after he leaves office next year.
* President Ramos has put a moratorium on issue of licences to operate new duty-free outlets in special economic zones.
* The Central Bank said the growth of loans extended by commercial banks slowed to 34.7 percent in April from 37.4 percent the previous month.
* Holding firm Filinvest Development Corp said its board had decided to participate in the privatisation of a Food Terminals Inc, a 121-hectare agro-industrial complex in suburban Manila.

* The exploration group of Shell Philippines Exploration BV and Occidental Philippines Inc said it had signed an MoU with National Power Corp to supply the state-owned firm with natural gas starting in the year 2002.

* A Reuters poll of six Manila brokerages showed the Philippines' largest conglomerate Ayala Corp should post a small rise in first-half profits with property remaining its mainstay despite fears over the sector.
* Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co said it produced a total of 1,128 kg of gold bullion and 582 kg of silver solutions in the first five months of the year.
* Metro Pacific Corp said its board had agreed to increase its stock dividend to 33 percent from the previous 30 percent declared on June 3.
* The Central Bank raised its special series three-month Treasury bill rate to 10.20 percent from 10.10 percent.
* TNT Express Worldwide, a unit of Dutch firm Koninklijke Ptt Netherland (KPN) wants to double its stake in Philippine cargo carrier Pacific East Asia Cargo Airlines (PEAC) from 20 percent.

* Philippine Tariff Commission chairman Emmanuel Velasco said the proposed tariff cut on the minimum volume of raw sugar imports allowed in the country would benefit food manufacturers. Velasco said the proposal to cut tariff on raw sugar imports under the minimum access volume to 20 percent from 50 percent starting July 1 has been sent to President Ramos for approval.
* Petrofields Exploration and Development Corp said its stake in the Etame oil exploration project in Gabon would be diluted with the entry of a new investor.
* The Social Security System (SSS) is looking for domestic and foreign portfolio managers to handle some of its 137.5 billion pesos in funds, SSS administrator Renato Valencia said.
* Newspaper Manila Bulletin said the Board of Investments plans to carry out a major overhaul of the Car Development Program that will further open up the local market to more car imports.
* The Inquirer newspaper said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) favoured the move of the government to extend an IMF-sponsored programme as this would give a positive signal to investors.
